prompt: a fresh blind critic (creative director and industrial designer), images only; the prompt is in this folder's README

stage1.impression: A red see-through box on a white sweep with a red horn floating above it. The insides show clearly and the red glow on the floor is pleasant, but the flat even light, the mottled side panel and the toy-like proportions make it read as a configurator render, not a campaign image.

The strongest frame. Low sun, the plaster wall, the walnut sideboard and green light on the floor give it a believable editorial mood. The speakers themselves look flat-fronted and boxy, though: dark outlines, a grille disc that seems pasted on and horns that hover. The room feels more real than the object.

A close-up of the formed horn: a glossy pink-red shell over the top of a cabinet. The rolled lip and the see-through shell look good, but the lumpy throat flange and the odd slanted post caps look modelled rather than made.

A smoked laminated horn whose stacked layers make a hypnotic contour-map tunnel. It is the one image that suggests a real design idea and a luxury object, although the even layer edges and the plain back are a little too perfect.

least_realistic.detail: The cabinet's edges and joints draw as near-black outlines, like an aluminium frame around green glass panels.
least_realistic.real_one_shows: In tinted cast acrylic the cut edges are the most saturated and brightest part: light travels along the sheet and leaves the polished edge as a glowing line, never neutral black.
least_realistic.how_made: Diamond- or flame-polish the edges; clear, bubble-free seams; let the edges show as glowing piping.

least_realistic.detail: The woofer's grille is a flat matte disc with no depth, mount or frame; it looks pasted on and blocks the view inside.
least_realistic.real_one_shows: Cloth on a thin ring with a visible edge, a slight dome from the tension, a gap and shadow from the baffle; or a mesh through which the cone shows faintly.
least_realistic.how_made: Cloth over a 3 mm laser-cut ring, held by hidden magnets in blind holes.

least_realistic.detail: The throat collar and flange round the compression driver is a lumpy blob with wavy outlines.
least_realistic.real_one_shows: A crisp machined adaptor: a turned ring, a flat bolt circle, four visible cap screws and a gasket line.
least_realistic.how_made: CNC-turn the throat adaptor; bolt it through a thickened boss with stainless M5 screws and nylon washers.

least_realistic.detail: The posts end in slanted bullet-shaped caps the horn's edge seems to rest on or pass through, with no visible fixing.
least_realistic.real_one_shows: A clear load path: a post threaded into a boss bonded under the horn, or a saddle the horn's curve sits in, an elastomer isolator at each contact.
least_realistic.how_made: Threaded stainless or bronze posts into bonded pads under the horn; rubber washers at both ends.

least_realistic.detail: Six thin rods hold the horn (four posts and two from the driver); they read as wires and the horn hovers.
least_realistic.real_one_shows: Two to four posts sized for a 5-10 kg horn and driver (12-16 mm), the signal wire inside one post.
least_realistic.how_made: Hollow tube posts with the cable inside, a connector at the top plate.

least_realistic.detail: The cabinet's right side is mottled and blotchy, unevenly dark top to bottom.
least_realistic.real_one_shows: A clean polished face with sharp reflections and colour that deepens evenly with angle.
least_realistic.how_made: More samples or less denoising in the render; physically, masking left on until assembly and a final polish.

least_realistic.detail: The woofer has a thick saturated bezel ring dyed the cabinet's colour, and a plain toy-like cone.
least_realistic.real_one_shows: A real pro woofer: a cast basket, a ribbed paper cone, a surround; a trim ring in its own material if any.
least_realistic.how_made: A recessed baffle with threaded inserts; the trim ring anodised or black, not the cabinet's tint.

least_realistic.detail: The lining and the crossover block read as lit solid lime plastic; the ports with square screwed flanges look like CAD library parts.
least_realistic.real_one_shows: White fibre in sheer sleeves stays soft and lighter than the tint; ports with flared ends in a baffle cutout.
least_realistic.how_made: Voile sleeves held with clear clips; flared port tubes.

least_realistic.detail: Every layer of the laminated horn has an identical perfect edge, no glue lines or misalignment; the back is a smooth shell.
least_realistic.real_one_shows: Faint bond lines, slight thickness variation, a stepped outside unless machined; edges glow brighter at the thin outer layers.
least_realistic.how_made: Rings cut from cast sheet, registered, bonded, then the bore machined and polished; show the steps or machine them away.

least_realistic.detail: A black power cable runs in plain view to the wall socket; the feet are tiny pins with no glides.
least_realistic.real_one_shows: A cable dressed out of sight from a bottom or rear exit; visible machined feet (cones or pucks with glides) at a scale for a heavy 1.3 m speaker.
least_realistic.how_made: A recessed rear connector pocket; four turned bronze feet on M8 inserts in a thickened bottom.

cooler.change: Make the laminated horn the signature and carry its stacked-layer language into the cabinet: a stack that steps down into the top plate, or cabinet edges built from visible laminations.
cooler.why: Image 4 is the only moment that looks like nothing else on the market; the contour turns the acoustics into a visible map.
cooler.risk: Cost, weight and bonding defects at luxury tolerance.

cooler.change: Integrate horn and cabinet as one silhouette: a top plate that rises into a cradle or saddle the horn sits in.
cooler.why: It reads as a PA horn bolted on a box; a continuous profile gives it presence.
cooler.risk: Decoupling and time alignment get harder.

cooler.change: Design for edge glow: thicker sheets with polished edges that collect light into bright tinted lines.
cooler.why: Edge glow, coloured shadows and caustics are the one thing only tinted cast acrylic can do.
cooler.risk: Weight and cost; internal lighting can look like a gaming accessory.

cooler.change: Treat the interior as a composed display: fewer deliberate parts on a grid, like a skeleton watch.
cooler.why: The transparency sells it, but now it shows a cluttered workshop.
cooler.risk: Constrains the acoustic layout; every assembly flaw shows.

cooler.change: Drop the flat opaque grille disc: an exposed woofer with a designed cone and trim, or a grille in the horn's tint.
cooler.why: The disc kills the see-through idea and looks generic.

horns.why: It turns the acoustic profile into a visible contour map with rhythm and depth, using what only stacked tinted cast acrylic can do, and gives a signature no PA horn has. The formed shell reads as a generic moulded horn, and its weak point, the throat collar, is where the eye goes.

reads_as_now: A clear acrylic box speaker with a translucent PA horn propped on thin rods: well rendered, but assembled rather than designed.
could_read_as: A glowing, sculptural piece of coloured light whose stacked-acrylic horn draws its own sound field, an object that would sit in a gallery as easily as in a listening room.
not_adopted: Two 'how made' notes conflict with the bonding research (R7, R8) and are not taken: solvent cement (Weld-On 4/16) for the joints (thick cast sheet takes polymerising cement), and dowel pins through the layers (they would show through the tint).
